items.text: Topos theory — 1
Four sessions on topoi, « or, as I like to see it, essentially on general topology ».
Prerequisites: topological spaces and continuous maps; the language of categories.
§ Review of sheaves on a topological space
Let $X$ be a topological space,
\mathcal O = \mathcal O(X) = \{\text{open subsets of } X\}
stable under arbitrary unions and finite intersections; ordered by inclusion.
An ordered set is a category:
\operatorname{Hom}(U,V)=\begin{cases}\varnothing & U\not\subset V\\ \{U\hookrightarrow V\} & U\subset V\end{cases}
Presheaves
A presheaf (of sets) on $X$: a contravariant functor
F\colon \mathcal O^{\mathrm{op}} \longrightarrow \mathbf{Sets}
U \mapsto F(U), \qquad U\subset V \;\mapsto\; \rho_{UV}\colon F(V)\to F(U) \quad\text{(restriction)}
U\subset V\subset W:\ \rho_{UW}=\rho_{UV}\circ\rho_{VW},\qquad \rho_{UU}=\mathrm{id}
\widehat{X} = \operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O^{\mathrm{op}},\mathbf{Sets})\quad\text{(category of presheaves)}
A morphism $f\colon F\to G$: maps $f_U\colon F(U)\to G(U)$ such that, for $U\subset V$,
\begin{CD} F(V) @>{f_V}>> G(V)\\ @V{\rho}VV @VV{\rho}V\\ F(U) @>{f_U}>> G(U) \end{CD}
commutes. Composition: $(g\circ f)_U = g_U\circ f_U$.
Sheaves
$F$ is separated if for every open $U$ and every covering $U=\bigcup_i U_i$ (i.e. $U=\sup_i U_i$ in $\mathcal O$),
F(U)\longrightarrow \prod_i F(U_i)\quad\text{is injective.}
Elements of $F(U)$: sections of $F$ over $U$; $\rho_{UV}(s)=s|_U$, the restriction of $s$ to $U$.
A family $(s_i)$, $s_i\in F(U_i)$, coming from a global section satisfies the necessary condition
s_i|_{U_i\cap U_j} = s_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}\qquad\forall\, i,j
$F$ is a sheaf if moreover the families satisfying it are exactly the image of $F(U)$:
F(U)\longrightarrow \prod_{i\in I}F(U_i)\;\rightrightarrows\;\prod_{(i,j)\in I\times I}F(U_i\cap U_j)\quad\text{exact}
« Exact »: the first arrow identifies $F(U)$ with the kernel of the double arrow, the elements with the same image under both.
Morphisms of sheaves: morphisms of the underlying presheaves.
\operatorname{Top}(X) \subset \widehat{X}\quad\text{full subcategory: the sheaves on } X
Examples
1. $E$ a set; $F(U)=E^U$, the maps $U\to E$; restriction of maps. A sheaf: the sheaf of maps from $X$ to $E$.
Subsheaves. $G\subset F$ if $G(U)\subset F(U)$ for all $U$, with the restrictions induced by those of $F$ — a subfunctor; that is, subsets $G(U)\subset F(U)$ stable under restriction.
If $F$ is a sheaf, a sub-presheaf $G$ is always separated; it is a sheaf iff « belonging to $G$ » is a property of local nature:
s\in G(U)\iff s|_{U_i}\in G(U_i)\ \ \forall i
2. $E$ a topological space: continuous maps $U\to E$ (continuity is local) — a subsheaf of 1.
3. $X$, $E$ differentiable manifolds ($C^\infty$ or $C^r$): differentiable maps $U\to E$. Likewise analytic varieties, analytic spaces…
4. A space over $X$: $p\colon E\to X$ continuous. Sections over $U$:
\Gamma(U,E/X)=\{\,s\colon U\to E \text{ continuous} : p\circ s = (U\hookrightarrow X)\,\}
Hence the word « sections » for the elements of $F(U)$.
(From the audience.) Example 2 is a case of 4: maps $U\to E$ = sections of $E\times X\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{pr}_2\ }X$.
5. $X$ locally compact: Radon measures on $U$. On $\mathbb R^n$, or a manifold: distributions — « distributions localize ».
6. $U\mapsto$ closed subsets of $U$, restriction by $Z\mapsto Z\cap V$. Likewise all subsets; analytic subsets of an analytic space.
« The language of sheaves is a very handy tool to deduce global information from local information. »
References: Godement, Topologie algébrique et théorie des faisceaux (Hermann); Bredon, Sheaf theory (McGraw-Hill).
Spaces over $X$ and their sheaves of sections
E\ \longmapsto\ \tilde E = \text{sheaf of (continuous) sections of } E \text{ over open sets of } X
Functorial: a morphism $f\colon E\to F$ over $X$ (the triangle commutes) gives
\tilde f\colon \tilde E\to\tilde F,\qquad \tilde f_U(s)=f\circ s
\operatorname{Esp}(X)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Top}(X),\qquad E\mapsto \tilde E
Question. Is this functor fully faithful — can $E$ be reconstructed from $\tilde E$?
No. Take $X=\{\mathrm{pt}\}$:
\operatorname{Esp}(\mathrm{pt}) \simeq \{\text{topological spaces}\}
\Gamma_U\colon \operatorname{Top}(X)\to\mathbf{Sets},\quad F\mapsto F(U);\qquad \Gamma(F)=F(X)
\Gamma\colon \operatorname{Top}(\mathrm{pt})\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\mathbf{Sets}
So $E\mapsto\tilde E$ becomes $E\mapsto$ the underlying set of $E$: the forgetful functor, which is not fully faithful — the topology is lost.
